The act of one who turns (rotates or twists).

examples.text: Still talking—more to herself than to the children—she swam into a majestical dance of the stateliest balancings, the haughtiest wheelings and turnings aside, the most dignified sinkings, the gravest risings, all joined together by the elaboratest interlacing steps and circles.
A doorknob of whatever roundish shape is effectively a continuum of levers, with the axis of the latching mechanism—known as the spindle—being the fulcrum about which the turning takes place.

glosses: One of the four eras, each lasting for about 21 years, that make up a saeculum according to the Strauss-Howe generational theory.

examples.text: Howe and Strauss predicted that in the Fourth Turning, Millennials would unite behind their president.

glosses: Shavings produced by turning something on a lathe.

examples.text: The turnings get into your trouser turnups!

glosses: present participle and gerund of turn

examples.text: The Earth is turning about its axis as we speak.
He made wooden soldiers by turning them on a hand lathe.

examples.text: [H]er mood, though consistently excited, was labile in affect, with sudden veerings from stormy hypomania to fearfulness and agitated depression.
